{{Short description|French clockmaker and amateur mathematician (1817–1878)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=March 2025}}
'''Louis Achille Brocot''' (pronounced "broco"<ref>[http://mb.nawcc.org/showthread.php?63437-Phonetic-blunder&p=471085&viewfull=1#post471085 Phonetic blunder]</ref>{{Better source needed|reason=The current source is insufficiently reliable ([[WP:NOTRS]]).|date=September 2026}}) (11 July 1817 – 19 January 1878) was a French [[clockmaker]]<ref name="britten">{{citation|title=Britten's Watch & Clock Makers' Handbook Dictionary & Guide|edition=15th|editor-first=J. W.|editor-last=Player|publisher=Taylor & Francis|page=380}}.</ref> and amateur mathematician.<ref name="mansuy">{{citation|title=Achille Brocot, mathématicien à ses heures|format = French|last=Mansuy|first=Roger|url=http://www.dma.ens.fr/culturemath/histoire%20des%20maths/htm/Brocot/Brocot.html|publisher=CultureMath}}.</ref>

He is known for his discovery (contemporaneously with, but independently of, German number theorist [[Moritz Stern]]) of the [[Stern–Brocot tree]], a mathematical structure useful in approximating [[real number]]s by [[rational number]]s; this sort of approximation is an important part of the design of [[gear ratio]]s for clocks.<ref>{{citation|first=Brian|last=Hayes|authorlink=Brian Hayes (scientist)|contribution=On the Teeth of Wheels|title=Group Theory in the Bedroom, and Other Mathematical Diversions|publisher=Hill and Wang|year=2008|url=http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/pub/on-the-teeth-of-wheels/}}.</ref>

Several improvements in clock design were attributed to Brocot. He invented the "Brocot Suspension", which enabled time keeping to be regulated by altering the length of the pendulum suspension spring by a key turned in the dial.[https://www.sellingantiques.co.uk/346340/superb%20victorian%20mantel%20clock%20achille%20brocot%20paris/]

He also made many practical horological innovations including refinement of his father Louis-Gabriel's [[pin-pallet escapement|Brocot escapement]] and the development of clocks with [[perpetual calendar]] mechanisms.<ref>{{citation|first=John G.|last=Kirk|title=The Brocots: A Dynasty of Horologers|url=http://www.nawcc69.org/pdf/Brocots_v3.pdf}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}. Powerpoint presentation based on {{harvtxt|Chavigny|1991}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|type =French|title=Les Brocot: une dynastie d'horlogers|first=Richard|last=Chavigny|publisher=Antoine Simonin|year=1991|isbn=978-2-88175-003-8}}.</ref> In order to commercially exploit his original designs, together with [[Jean-Baptiste Delettrez]] he established the clockmaking company "Brocot & Delettrez" in Paris on 20 October 1851, a partnership that would continue until his death.
